pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go (1 mark)
   A. Faster and further
   B. Not move
   C. Change colour
   D. Slower

2. A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Increases speed
   B. Holds objects together
   C. Decreases speed
   D. Starts motion

3. What effect of force is shown when a goalkeeper stops a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Changes its colour
   B. Stops a moving object
   C. Makes it lighter
   D. Starts a moving object

4. Which of these is a push? (1 mark)
   A. Pulling a cart
   B. Kicking a football
   C. Drawing water with a rope
   D. Opening a drawer by its handle

5. Which is a use of gravity? (1 mark)
   A. Water flowing downhill
   B. Making objects float in air
   C. Making air hot
   D. Lifting up a stone by itself

6. Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving it dry and rusty
   B. Oiling it
   C. Adding sand
   D. Wetting it with mud

7. The moon shines brightly at night. Why is it still not a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. It is cold
   B. It is too small
   C. It is too near
   D. It reflects light from the sun

8. Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin? (1 mark)
   A. Paraffin lamp
   B. Sun
   C. Star
   D. Lightning

9. What is a transparent material? (1 mark)
   A. A material that is always red
   B. A material that blocks all light
   C. A material that lets almost all light pass through
   D. A material that makes light

10. Which artificial light uses energy from the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Candle
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Paraffin lamp
   D. Firewood

11. Which of these is a safe practice with light? (1 mark)
   A. Stare at bright lights
   B. Look at the sun with your eyes
   C. Never look straight at the sun
   D. Shine torches in eyes

12. Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night? (1 mark)
   A. To scare away wild animals
   B. To warm animals
   C. To make animals heavier
   D. To make animals sleepy

13. Which of these is NOT a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A candle
   B. A torch
   C. An electric bulb
   D. A mirror

14. What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do? (1 mark)
   A. Make sound
   B. Make their own light all night
   C. Make heat
   D. Shine when car lights fall on them

15. Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light? (1 mark)
   A. Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   B. A ruler only
   C. A cup of water
   D. A bell

16. Which of these is NOT a source of heat? (1 mark)
   A. A burning log
   B. A cold stone in the shade
   C. The sun
   D. A kettle

17. Why is cooking food useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food raw
   B. It makes food cold
   C. It makes food dirty
   D. It makes food soft and safer to eat

18. Which instrument measures temperature? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Balance
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Thermometer

19. Which of these helps to prevent burns? (1 mark)
   A. Touching hot pots
   B. Holding hot handles
   C. Using gloves
   D. Playing near fire

20. In the water cycle, what does heat from the sun do? (1 mark)
   A. Removes all water
   B. Turns water into vapour
   C. Makes water heavy
   D. Freezes water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State two uses of heat at home. (2 marks)

22. Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects. (3 marks)

23. Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each. (4 marks)

24. Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home. (4 marks)

25. Give three safety measures to observe when cooking. (3 marks)

26. Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions. (5 marks)

27. Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth. (3 marks)

28. What should you do for a small burn? State three actions. (3 marks)

29. Give three uses of friction in daily life. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Faster and further
   A stronger force has a bigger effect.

2. C — Decreases speed
   Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

3. B — Stops a moving object
   The force of the hands stops the ball.

4. B — Kicking a football
   A kick pushes the ball.

5. A — Water flowing downhill
   Gravity makes water flow downhill.

6. B — Oiling it
   Oil helps parts slide.

7. D — It reflects light from the sun
   The moon does not make its own light.

8. A — Paraffin lamp
   A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

9. C — A material that lets almost all light pass through
   Transparent materials let us see clearly through them.

10. B — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp charges by day.

11. C — Never look straight at the sun
   Looking at the sun harms eyes.

12. A — To scare away wild animals
   Bright lights can scare away predators.

13. D — A mirror
   A mirror only reflects light.

14. D — Shine when car lights fall on them
   Reflectors bounce light back.

15. A — Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

16. B — A cold stone in the shade
   A cold stone gives out no heat of its own.

17. D — It makes food soft and safer to eat
   Heat kills many germs.

18. D — Thermometer
   A thermometer shows how hot something is.

19. C — Using gloves
   Gloves give protection.

20. B — Turns water into vapour
   Heat causes evaporation from seas and rivers.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cooking, warming, ironing, drying clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with reason.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use gloves, turn handles inwards, keep children away, do not play with matches, keep paraffin away from fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
